children: Pilgrim's Pride has formed a special committee of independent directors to consider an unsolicited bid from the world's largest meatpacking company JBS.
In mid-August, JBS, which currently owns about 82% of Pilgrim's common stock, made the proposal that would give Pilgrim's Pride shareholders exposure to a bigger and more diversified global business.

Pilgrim's Pride operates protein processing plants and prepared-foods facilities focusing on poultry products in 14 states, Puerto Rico and Mexico, as well as in Europe, employing around 63,000 people across its operations.

JBS proposed a fixed exchange ratio of about 2.1 shares of its Class A common stock for each share of Pilgrim's Pride's common stock, based on the Aug. 18 closing prices of $13.66 and $28.49, respectively.

Pilgrim's Pride said its board won't approve any transaction without the favorable recommendation of the special committee, and also cautioned that there couldn't be any assurance that any particular outcome.
